lessons.context: Teach the human heart: what it does, its main parts (atria, ventricles, valves), and why exercise matters. Use one short relatable story or analogy. Keep it simple and warm.
lessons.greeting: Namaste! I am Maya. Today we will discover the human heart together. Are you ready?
lessons.subject: Science

visuals.caption: Your heart is a pump made of muscle, about the size of your fist. It has 4 chambers — 2 atria on top, 2 ventricles below — beating about 100,000 times every day.
visuals.label: The whole heart

visuals.caption: Valves are like one-way doors! They open to let blood flow forward, then close so it cannot flow back. This keeps blood moving in the right direction.
visuals.label: Valves

visuals.caption: Blood travels in a big loop: body → heart → lungs → heart → body. Red brings fresh oxygen out; blue carries used blood back for more oxygen.
visuals.label: Blood's journey
